body:
Fiona McCarthy  1731091129
Pulling folks in here re: Safe apply + rollback. We need to lock down RBAC + audit logging semantics before implementation lands. Specifically:
- what audit events are mandatory + immutable
- what fields are allowed/required vs must be redacted
- retention expectations for enterprise (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)

@Marcus Lin @Kevin Osei @Kaitlyn Nguyen @Chloe Martin @Dylan Brooks @Svetlana Petrenko @Allison Grant

Marcus Lin  1731091398
:+1: starting point from Security Eng side:
1) Audit logs must be append-only / immutable. “Update” is not allowed; corrections should be a new event referencing the prior event_id.
2) We need to log *attempted* actions in addition to successful ones (incl authz denials), otherwise there’s no forensic trail.

For this feature I’d consider these as mandatory event types:
- optimize_config.apply_attempted
- optimize_config.apply_succeeded
- optimize_config.apply_failed
- optimize_config.rollback_attempted
- optimize_config.rollback_succeeded
- optimize_config.rollback_failed
- optimize_config.preflight_run (and preflight_failed if we treat that as distinct)
- optimize_config.permission_denied (or generic authz_denied but with resource context)

Kevin Osei  1731091604
Agree on append-only. On retention: enterprise customers keep asking for 1y minimum, but regulated (banking) will push for 7y.
My suggestion:
- default retention: 400 days (gives “1 year + buffer”)
- enterprise add-on: configurable up to 7 years
- for Private: make it “customer-controlled retention” but we should still document a recommended baseline.

Also: audit export to SIEM needs to be in scope at least for “event schema stable + correlation id + tenant id”.

Kaitlyn Nguyen  1731091812
RBAC side: we’re adding permissions:
- optimize.config.apply
- optimize.config.rollback
- optimize.config.view_history (maybe separate from apply/rollback)

We should also think about: who can view audit logs? Today “audit.log.read” is gated heavily.
If Console is going to deep link from version history -> audit entry, we’ll need a UX fallback when user lacks audit permissions.

Chloe Martin  1731092190
From Console backend POV we’re emitting audit events via the central audit service. Questions we need answered:
- required fields for each event (actor + scope + version ids)
- do we log the full config blob? (please no, but need clarity)
- if we can’t log full diff, can we log a “diff summary”?

Right now our proto payload includes:
- tenant_id
- environment (hosted/dedicated/private)
- scope key (customer_id/region/cluster/route/model)
- from_version_id / to_version_id
- request_id / idempotency_key
- actor_user_id + actor_email
- source (console/api/automation)
- linked_ticket (optional)
- reason (freeform)

Dylan Brooks  1731092447
+1. Also note UX wants to show “who changed what” in history. If audit doesn’t contain enough, we’ll be tempted to overload version metadata.
We need a clean split:
- version store = immutable config + metadata for product UX
- audit log = security record of action attempts/outcomes

Re: “what changed”: we can show a computed diff in Console without storing it in audit, as long as we have from/to version pointers.

Allison Grant  1731092716
Observability note: if we want incident-bot/deploy-bot to post links, the audit event needs a stable event_id and correlation_id that can be joined with runtime propagation metrics.

Also strongly prefer:
- do not log raw prompts, headers, or request payloads
- if we need to link, log hashes/ids (request_id, rollout_id)

Svetlana Petrenko  1731092982
For SIEM export, most customers want:
- actor identity (human vs service account)
- originating IP (if available) + user_agent for Console actions
- “where applied” scope (tenant + region/cluster)
- outcome + error code

But they *don’t* want prompt/config content in the SIEM stream (it becomes a data handling nightmare).

Devon Price  1731093249
From incident-bot side, we can post:
- “config change detected” with version_id + scope + who
- deep link to Console history + audit event
- on failure, post the error summary + runbook link

But I need a guaranteed identifier to put in the message that users can hand to on-call. Correlation ID seems right.

Fiona McCarthy  1731093521
Ok, let’s pin down the redaction rules explicitly.

Security requirements I’m hearing:
- Immutable append-only audit record
- Log attempts + denies
- No raw config blobs / no secrets

But I want a crisp list: what fields are ALWAYS safe, what fields are CONDITIONALLY safe, what fields are NEVER allowed.

Marcus Lin  1731093893
Proposal (feel free to nitpick):

ALWAYS (required):
- event_id, event_ts
- tenant_id
- actor_type (user/service), actor_id, actor_display (email ok), authn_method (SSO/API token)
- action (apply/rollback/preflight)
- outcome (attempted/succeeded/failed/denied)
- resource_type=optimize_config
- scope identifiers (customer_id, deployment_mode, region, cluster, route_id, model_id) as applicable
- from_version_id / to_version_id (or target_version_id)
- request_id + idempotency_key

CONDITIONALLY:
- source_ip, user_agent (only for Console / interactive)
- linked_ticket (Jira/Linear URL)
- reason (freeform) -> but needs guardrails (see below)
- error_message (truncate + sanitize)

NEVER:
- full config JSON
- raw diff with values
- secrets/keys
- prompt text, customer data, tokens

On “reason” field: we should cap length, and maybe add a UI hint “don’t paste sensitive data”. We should also consider a server-side regex scrub for obvious secret patterns.

Kevin Osei  1731094210
:+1: on server-side scrub. We’ve been burned by people pasting stack traces containing headers.

Also: for error_message, suggest we store:
- error_code (enum)
- error_class (e.g. VALIDATION_FAILED, PROPAGATION_TIMEOUT, AUTHZ_DENIED)
- error_detail (optional, truncated to ~1KB, with scrubbing)

That’s usually enough for enterprise reporting and avoids accidental leakage.

Chloe Martin  1731094536
This works. Implementation detail: the preflight validator currently produces warnings like “batch.max_batch_tokens exceeds recommended bound for model family.”
Is that considered safe to include in audit logs? It’s not customer data, but it’s “operational detail.”

Marcus Lin  1731094774
Validator warnings should be ok to log if:
- no raw config values (or only bounded numeric values)
- no tenant data

But we should treat it as “operational metadata” and still sanitize. My preference:
- store warning codes + short messages
- keep the full verbose report in internal logs (non-audit) gated by admin access

Allison Grant  1731095067
Agree. Also want audit to stay small; if we jam a big warning report it becomes expensive + noisy.

Suggest:
- audit has `preflight_summary=PASS/WARN/FAIL`, `warning_codes=[...]`
- Console can fetch the detailed preflight report from the versioning service (not from audit), and that endpoint can enforce stricter permissions.

Kaitlyn Nguyen  1731095388
On RBAC + audit interplay:
- We should audit `permission_denied` for apply/rollback attempts.
- For viewing history: I’d rather not produce an audit event for every “read history page” (too chatty), but we *should* audit access to raw audit logs if we expose them.

Also, we need to define roles:
- SRE Oncall: can rollback + view history in prod
- Platform Operator: can apply + rollback
- Read-only: view history only

Enterprise: default is “deny rollback” unless explicitly granted.

Dylan Brooks  1731095712
This aligns with product ask: rollback is powerful, should be “break glass” for some tenants.

Question: do we require a justification string for rollback? UX wants it optional but encouraged.

Fiona McCarthy  1731095940
For enterprise, rollback justification is a common ask (change management). I’m ok with:
- required for rollback in prod scopes (Hosted prod, Dedicated prod clusters, Private prod env)
- optional in dev/staging

But we need to ensure the justification field follows the same scrub/limits as “reason”.

Kevin Osei  1731096261
Retention policy wording suggestion for PRD/ADR:
- Audit logs are immutable and retained for a minimum of 400 days for enterprise plans.
- Longer retention up to 7 years available for compliance add-on.
- Private deployments: retention is configurable by customer; Redwood recommends >= 400 days and provides tooling to export to customer SIEM.

Also: deletion. If a customer requests deletion (GDPR), we should clarify that audit logs are generally exempt as “security records,” but we may need to pseudonymize actor_display if it’s personal data.

Marcus Lin  1731096599
Yep. We should explicitly avoid storing personal data beyond what we need:
- actor_email is often requested, but if we store both actor_id and email, we can later rotate email display name without changing the immutable event (hm… conflict).

Alternative:
- store actor_id as canonical
- store actor_email as “display” with note it may be stale

But we cannot mutate historic events. So: keep actor_id as required, email as optional.

Svetlana Petrenko  1731096907
For SIEM exports, customers frequently expect email. If we only export actor_id, it’s not useful.
Maybe we store both but document that email is captured at event time and is immutable.

Also: for service accounts, export a name like “svc-optimize-automation” not a random UUID.

Kaitlyn Nguyen  1731097255
We can do:
- actor_id (uuid)
- actor_label (string) -> either email or service account name

And in RBAC service we already have “principal display name” concept.

Chloe Martin  1731097548
Another question: do we need to log *config diff metadata* like “fields changed”? That would help “who changed what” without values.
E.g. changed_keys=["batching.max_concurrency", "quantization.profile"]

Is that allowed in audit?

Marcus Lin  1731097810
Changed keys list is ok IMO. It’s not the values. It can still leak some info (“they use quantization”), but that’s generally fine at tenant admin level.
If we’re worried, only include it for users with appropriate permission (but audit events aren’t per-user filtered usually).

Maybe the rule is:
- changed_keys list allowed
- values not allowed

Allison Grant  1731098092
From tooling perspective, changed_keys is gold for alert routing (“quantization changed” should page different folks than “cache toggle changed”).

Devon Price  1731098278
If we have changed_keys, incident-bot can include a lightweight summary in Slack:
“Rollback executed (quantization + batching knobs).”

Fiona McCarthy  1731098613
Ok, converging. Action items:
1) @Marcus Lin can you draft the audit event schema section (mandatory fields + redaction rules + immutability statement)?
2) @Kaitlyn Nguyen please confirm RBAC permissions + default role mapping proposal (esp. Dedicated/Private).
3) @Chloe Martin / @Dylan Brooks make sure Console collects “reason/linked ticket” and displays a “don’t paste secrets” warning.
4) @Kevin Osei draft retention policy text for enterprise + private.

One last thing: where do we store audit logs to satisfy immutability? (I know we already have the audit service, but we should state the guarantees.)

Kevin Osei  1731098926
Audit service is already “write-once” from app POV; we can state:
- events are stored append-only, no update/delete API
- access is tightly RBAC’d
- encryption at rest

If we need stronger “WORM” wording, we can add: “logical immutability” (no mutation via application) and rely on infra controls + backups. I can sync with platform if we need compliance-grade language.

Marcus Lin  1731099310
I’ll draft wording with “append-only, no mutation operations supported, corrections via compensating events.”

Also: can we ensure audit events include the *runtime propagation result*? That’s important for forensics (“applied in us-east but stuck in eu-west”).

Chloe Martin  1731099629
We can emit multiple events:
- apply_attempted (control plane accepted)
- apply_succeeded (propagation completed to all targets)
- apply_failed (propagation failure with partial status)

For “partial”, we can include counts only: target_total, target_succeeded, target_failed. Not listing specific nodes.

Allison Grant  1731099868
Counts are good. If we want node-level, keep it in internal logs/metrics.

Fiona McCarthy  1731100264
Perfect. Let’s proceed with counts only in audit. Node-level is too sensitive + too big.

Closing this out; please post drafts back in this thread when ready. :lock:

Marcus Lin  1731100876
Noted. I’ll post schema draft tomorrow AM and tag for review.
